Rav Huna: I had no [wine for] kiddush, so I pawned my belt and brought kiddush with it
Rav to Rav Huna: may it be [God's] will that you be wrapped in silk

Rav, annoyed: why did you not say to me, when I blessed you, 'and likewise to the Master'?

R' Elazar ben Shammua: and I never strode over the heads of the holy people
R' Elazar ben Shammua: and I never raised my hands [in the priestly blessing] without a blessing
R' Perida: in all my days no man preceded me to the beit midrash
R' Perida: and I never led the blessing in the presence of a kohen

R' Yochanan (via R' Yitzchak): it is forbidden to eat of an animal whose gifts have not been separated
R' Yitzchak: whoever eats of an animal whose gifts have not been separated is as if he eats tevel
and the halakha is not as he [R' Yitzchak] says

R' Yochanan's verse: 'all who hate me love death' (Prov 8:36) -- read not 'who hate me' but 'who make me hated'
R' Nechunya ben HaKana: in all my days I was never honoured through my fellow's disgrace
R' Nechunya ben HaKana: and my fellow's curse never went up with me onto my bed
R' Nechunya ben HaKana: and I was openhanded with my money
the Gemara: 'never honoured through my fellow's disgrace' -- like Rav Huna, who carried a hoe on his shoulder
Rav Huna to Rav Chana bar Chanilai, who took the hoe from him: if you are used to carrying in your own town, carry; if not, being honoured through your disgrace does not please me
the Gemara: 'my fellow's curse never went up onto my bed' -- like Mar Zutra
Mar Zutra, when he went up to his bed, would say: I forgive whoever has vexed me
the Gemara: 'openhanded with my money' -- as the Master said: Iyov was openhanded with his money
the Master: Iyov was openhanded with his money, for he would leave a peruta of his money with the shopkeeper
the verse of the daily offering: 'one lamb' (Num 28:4)
R' Nechunya HaGadol to his attendants who were beating R' Akiva: he is a young scholar, leave him
R' Nechunya HaGadol: 'one' -- the choicest of its flock
R' Nechunya HaGadol: in all my days I never accepted gifts
R' Nechunya HaGadol: and I never stood on my measures [exacted my due]
R' Nechunya HaGadol: and I was openhanded with my money
the Gemara: 'never accepted gifts' -- like R' Elazar
R' Elazar: when they sent him gifts from the Nasi's house he did not take them; when they invited him he did not go
R' Elazar: does it not please you that I should live? as it is written: 'he who hates gifts shall live' (Prov 15:27)
R' Zeira: when they sent him [gifts] from the Nasi's house he did not take them; when they invited him he went
R' Zeira: they are honoured by me
Rava: whoever passes over his measures -- all his transgressions are passed over
Rava's verse: 'He bears iniquity and passes over transgression' (Micah 7:18) -- for whom does He bear iniquity? for him who passes over transgression
to RYbK's 'are you weary of my life?', Rebbi: my master, it is Torah, and I must learn
R' Yehoshua ben Korcha: in all my days I never gazed at the likeness of a wicked man
R' Yochanan: it is forbidden for a person to gaze at the image of the likeness of a wicked man

R' Elazar: [one who gazes at a wicked man] -- his eyes grow dim

the Gemara: this and that [both] caused it
Rava: [the prohibition on gazing at a wicked man is] from here: 'to lift the face of the wicked is not good' (Prov 18:5)

the other said: may [good] come to me, for I never made a partnership with a gentile

nodes.label_en: R' Zeira: and I never walked four cubits without Torah and without tefillin

nodes.label_he: ולא ששתי בתקלת חבירי
nodes.label_en: R' Zeira: and I never rejoiced at my fellow's stumbling

nodes.label_he: ולא קראתי לחבירי בחניכתו
nodes.label_en: R' Zeira: and I never called my fellow by his [derogatory] nickname
